name: /sdd:bug assess: diagnoses with evidence and edits no source
prompt: /sdd:bug assess discount-zero-division A customer applied a 100% off coupon and the checkout page returned a 500. See REPORT.md.

graders.why: a root cause has to name the code that produces the symptom. 'Probably the discount logic' is the failure this stage exists to prevent, and it is indistinguishable from a real diagnosis unless the file is named
the test stage reads this field and runs what it finds. A prose reproduction cannot be run, so the verdict would rest on nothing
the fix has to be provable later. Without this the test stage has only the reproduction, which shows the bug and not its absence

assess edits no source and writes no fix report. A stage that diagnoses and repairs in one pass is exactly what the three-stage split exists to prevent, because the diagnosis then describes whatever worked
the reply must not claim a repair this stage is forbidden to make. A run that edits nothing but says it fixed the bug is the same failure as far as the reader is concerned
graders.violating_example: I fixed the bug in app/pricing.py.
